title: fix(kernel): make STEP pcurves on the solidcore kernel
body:
## What changed

This PR moves the solidcore pin and lets the solidcore kernel make the pcurves (2D trims) that a STEP file does not give. It is part A of #917. Part B (the importer switch) stacks on this PR.

- `Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock`: the solidcore pin moves from `55d0e76` to `2016386442dfee3b2a0c3a1bfdd4017c5254dac8` (the fork sync of 2026-11-19).
- `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_trims.rs` (new, with `solidcore_trims/checks.rs`): `KernelTrims` implements the solidcore `Trims` seam. It makes each pcurve on the kernel. It measures the gap of each bare edge to its face, and refuses an edge that is more than `MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM` = 0.01 mm off its face. The tolerance in the file does not change this cap.
  - The lift check holds a made pcurve to the edge's tolerance, but never to more than `MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM`.
  - A face, edge or vertex tolerance that is not a finite number of zero or more is refused by name. A lift sample whose distance is not finite is refused by name. (`f64::max` drops a NaN, so each value is checked before it is used.)
- `docs/decisions/917-kernel-pcurves.md`: the decisions and the dropped options.

## Readings

| Fixture | Edge gap | Verdict on this branch |
|---|---|---|
| fig8 | 3.5e-12 mm | agree |
| fillet_corner | 8.2e-13 mm | watertight, within tolerance (truck mesh is open: 121 open edges) |
| bar_cross_holes | 1.19e-6 mm | watertight, within tolerance (truck mesh is open: 1090 open edges) |
| bspline_discontinuous | 0.25 mm | refused (see below) |
| twisted_flank (new, our own) | does not reach KernelTrims: the reader makes its pcurves | read |
| Milling-test, Milling-test-inch | - | agree (was "disagree: bounding box"; the port's box at 2016386 stops at the flat, Refs #939) |

**Which fixtures reach KernelTrims.** A probe (removed before the commit) showed that fillet_corner, bar_cross_holes and fig8 reach it, and bspline_discontinuous reaches it until the gap cap refuses it. The two twisted_flank files do not reach it. `step_closed_form.rs` pins the KernelTrims route. The gate map line of `step_twisted_flank.rs` now says this.

**The lift tolerance.** The lift check uses `min(held, MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM)`. The held tolerances on the fixtures are 1e-6 mm (fillet_corner) and 2e-5 mm (bar_cross_holes), under the cap, so no verdict changes. The largest lift gaps are at most 2.9e-7 mm (fillet_corner) and 1.2e-5 mm (bar_cross_holes). All volumes stay the same and the two refused fixtures stay refused. The decision file records the readings.

**bspline_discontinuous stays refused.** The rule is the cap `MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM` = 0.01 mm in `cover_gaps` (`crates/kernel/src/solidcore_trims.rs`). The refusal text is: `#16 at read: pcurves failed on 1 of 6 faces; first: face #53: kernel pcurves: edge 0 lies 0.2500 mm off the face's surface, over the cap of 0.01 mm`. The pin is `step_twisted_flank::an_edge_a_quarter_millimetre_off_its_face_is_refused_by_name`, and the `step_agreement` row is "both refuse".

**Independent volume tests** (`crates/kernel/tests/step_closed_form.rs`). Each test compares the kernel's exact volume with a closed form that comes from the fixture's own dimensions (rel 1e-5), and checks the box (1e-6) and solidcore's own closed mesh (rel 1e-3):
- `fillet_corner_reads_at_its_closed_form_volume`: closed form 26816.4939 mm3, reading 26816.49 mm3.
- `bar_cross_holes_reads_at_its_closed_form_volume`: closed form 78225.6805 mm3, reading 78225.68 mm3.
- `fillet_corner_in_inches_reads_at_its_closed_form_volume_in_mm`: the test changes the length unit of `fillet_corner.step` to the inch in memory. The volume is 25.4^3 times the closed form, in mm, and the box is +-381 mm.

## Port pins that the pin move changed (re-triage)

The cause of all three is the solidcore move `55d0e76` -> `2016386`. KernelTrims is not the cause: none of these tests reads STEP.

1. `blend`: the rim chamfer's default path now gives the cone (upstream WR-421, solidcore#420). The test `not_yet_rim_chamfer_default_path_stays_a_finding` asked for a promotion. It is now `rim_chamfer_default_path_matches_the_cone`. This test heals the result to a closed solid and measures it against the cone's closed form (volume and box).
2. `corrupt_input`: "box at NaN origin" changes from "Ok non-solid" to "Err". The refusal is the stricter verdict. The pin is now "Err", with a comment that names the rev. The other 14 rows do not change.
3. `import_corpus`: the writer now prints the zone tolerance as `1e-5`, not `0.0000100000000000`. The literal corpus edit changed nothing, so the zero, negative and NaN rows read the intact box. The reader does not accept a NaN tolerance: `read_smb` refuses a non-finite tolerance by name. The edit now finds the header line by its label. The corpus test asserts that each edit changes the file. The new test `non_finite_zone_tolerance_is_refused_by_name` asserts the refusal text for NaN, inf and -inf. All rows of `KNOWN_SMB_VERDICTS` keep their pins.

No test was deleted, ignored or loosened. The `#[test]` count goes up by 11: three in `step_closed_form`, three in `step_twisted_flank`, two in `step_agreement` (`per_file!` rows `step_twisted_flank` and `step_twisted_flank_off`), one in `import_corpus`, and two unit tests in `solidcore_trims/checks.rs` (`a_lift_sample_that_is_not_finite_is_refused_by_name`, `a_tolerance_that_is_not_finite_is_refused_by_name`).
